scale: Best in class: nothing a top product designer would change.
Decent, but clearly unpolished in places.
Poor: the design gets in the way of the task.

categories.name: Hierarchy and focus
categories.description: The most important content and actions stand out; grouping and reading order are clear; nothing competes for attention without a reason.

categories.name: Layout and spacing
categories.description: Alignment, a consistent spacing rhythm, sensible use of space and a density that suits the task; no awkward gaps or crowding.

categories.name: Typography
categories.description: A clear type scale, suitable sizes and weights, comfortable line length and height, legible small text, and monospace only where it helps.

categories.name: Color and contrast
categories.description: A coherent palette with enough contrast in every theme shown; color carries meaning and emphasis rather than decoration; neither garish nor washed out.

categories.name: Components and states
categories.description: Controls look like what they do (buttons, links, inputs, switches); statuses and badges read at a glance; empty, error and loading states are designed, not left plain.

categories.name: Consistency
categories.description: The same kind of thing looks and is named the same across screens and themes; radii, borders, icons, spacing and labels follow one system.

categories.name: Small screens
categories.description: Phone layouts reflow cleanly, keep tap targets usable and text readable, and nothing overflows or hides essential information.

categories.name: Polish
categories.description: Details are finished: optical alignment, truncation, borders, icon quality, visible focus and hover hints; the whole feels deliberate.
